sources.chunk_text:
## 2. Physical Specifications

The Nebula Pro measures 84 mm wide, 84 mm tall and 22 mm deep, and weighs 210
grams without the mounting plate. The display is a 4-inch IPS panel with a
resolution of 480 by 480 pixels. The housing is flame-retardant polycarbonate
with a brushed aluminium front ring. The wall plate requires a standard UK or
EU single-gang back box.

## 1. Product Overview

The Nebula Pro Smart Thermostat is a wall-mounted climate controller designed
for residential heating systems. It combines a rotary dial with a 4-inch
touchscreen and learns the household's routine over a two-week calibration
period. The unit is manufactured by Halcyon Home Systems and sold through
authorised retailers and the Halcyon online store.

## 3. Electrical Requirements

The Nebula Pro is designed for low-voltage HVAC systems only. It must be
connected to 24 VAC power and requires a C-wire (common wire). It is NOT
compatible with high-voltage systems running 110 V or 240 V mains directly.
Installing the unit on a high-voltage circuit will permanently damage the
device and voids the warranty. A licensed electrician should perform the
installation if a C-wire is not present at the thermostat location.

To reset the Nebula Pro to factory settings, hold the rotary dial for 15
seconds until the LED flashes amber three times. Releasing the dial after
the amber pattern begins erases all schedules, Wi-Fi credentials, and the
calibration history. A factory reset does not deregister the device from the
Nebula Home app; use the "remove device" option for that.

follows the suggested schedules.

available for iOS 16 and later and Android 12 and later. The app stores
temperature history for 12 months and supports geofencing, so the heating
drops to the away temperature when the last household member leaves.

records.question: How long did the Project Meridian field study run?
records.answer: The Project Meridian field study ran for 13 weeks, from June 2 to August 29, 2025 [Source 1].

sources.chunk_text:
## Study Overview

Project Meridian investigated whether continuous soil moisture sensing could
reduce water use without lowering crop yield on medium-sized farms. The study
ran for 13 weeks, from June 2 to August 29, 2025, across three farms in the
central valley region.

# Project Meridian - Research Notes

Kestrel Agricultural Institute - Field Science Division
Study period: Q3 2025

2. RESPONSE TIMES

Critical incidents receive a first response within 2 hours, around the
clock. Standard incidents receive a first response within 1 business day.
Low-priority questions receive a first response within 3 business days.
These targets are measured from the moment a ticket is created in the
support portal.

## 10. Energy Saving

Halcyon's internal field study of 2,100 households found that homes using the
Nebula Pro adaptive scheduling saved up to 14% on heating bills over a full
year. Savings depend on insulation, climate, and how closely the household
follows the suggested schedules.

## Funding and Personnel

The work was supported by a $120,000 grant from the GreenAcre Foundation
(grant number GA-2025-114). The lead researcher was Dr. Lena Okafor, with
field coordination by Marcus Webb and sensor engineering by Priya Raman. Two
graduate interns from the institute's agronomy programme assisted with plot
measurements.

records.question: How often did the SM-100 sensor record soil moisture?
records.answer: The SM-100 sensor recorded volumetric water content every 15 minutes [Source 1].

sources.chunk_text:
## Equipment

Each managed plot was fitted with an SM-100 soil dielectric moisture sensor
buried 25 cm deep in the root zone. The sensor recorded volumetric water
content every 15 minutes and transmitted readings over LoRaWAN to a local
gateway. Control plots were irrigated on the farm's traditional schedule with
no sensing equipment.

## Study Overview

Project Meridian investigated whether continuous soil moisture sensing could
reduce water use without lowering crop yield on medium-sized farms. The study
ran for 13 weeks, from June 2 to August 29, 2025, across three farms in the
central valley region.

## Publication

A manuscript describing the trial was submitted to the Journal of Applied
Agronomy in October 2025 under the title "Soil moisture sensing as an early
drought warning system in medium-scale maize farming". A follow-up trial
covering a full growing season is planned for 2026, pending additional
funding.

## Early Stress Detection

The most striking observation was an early warning effect: the sensor network
detected the onset of drought stress 9 days before visual symptoms such as
leaf rolling appeared in the control plots. This lead time allowed targeted
irrigation that avoided a projected yield loss during the July heatwave.

## Irrigation Protocol

Sensor-managed plots were irrigated only when the average volumetric water
content of the top 40 cm fell below a threshold set at 35 percent of field
capacity. Control plots followed each farm's conventional calendar. Irrigation
events and volumes were logged automatically by the farm gate controllers.

records.question: What was the average yield improvement in the sensor-managed plots?
records.answer: The average yield improvement in the sensor-managed plots was 11.4% compared to the paired controls, measured as dry grain mass per hectare at harvest [Source 1].

sources.chunk_text:
## Results

The average yield improvement in sensor-managed plots was 11.4% compared to
the paired controls, measured as dry grain mass per hectare at harvest. Water
use in sensor-managed plots fell by 23% over the same period. The largest
relative gain appeared on Farm B, where the silty clay loam drained fastest
between irrigation events.

## Irrigation Protocol

Sensor-managed plots were irrigated only when the average volumetric water
content of the top 40 cm fell below a threshold set at 35 percent of field
capacity. Control plots followed each farm's conventional calendar. Irrigation
events and volumes were logged automatically by the farm gate controllers.

## Experimental Design

The trial used 48 experimental plots in total: 24 sensor-managed plots and 24
control plots, matched in pairs by soil type and crop variety. The plots were
split across three farms: Farm A on sandy loam, Farm B on silty clay loam, and
Farm C on clay. Each plot measured 0.4 hectares and was planted with the same
drought-tolerant maize hybrid.

## Equipment

Each managed plot was fitted with an SM-100 soil dielectric moisture sensor
buried 25 cm deep in the root zone. The sensor recorded volumetric water
content every 15 minutes and transmitted readings over LoRaWAN to a local
gateway. Control plots were irrigated on the farm's traditional schedule with
no sensing equipment.

## Statistical Analysis

Data were analysed with a mixed-effects model treating farm as a random
effect and irrigation strategy as a fixed effect. The yield difference was
significant at p < 0.01. A sensitivity analysis excluding the heatwave week
reduced the yield improvement estimate to 8.2%, which remains significant at
p < 0.05.

records.question: How much less water did the sensor-managed plots use?
records.answer: The sensor-managed plots used 23% less water over the same period [Source 1].

## 11. Sensors and Accuracy

The built-in temperature sensor is accurate to plus or minus 0.3 degrees
Celsius, and the humidity sensor to plus or minus 2 percent. Two remote
sensor jacks are available for rooms with uneven heating. The thermostat
averages the readings of all connected sensors when more than one is
detected.

## Results

The average yield improvement in sensor-managed plots was 11.4% compared to
the paired controls, measured as dry grain mass per hectare at harvest. Water
use in sensor-managed plots fell by 23% over the same period. The largest
relative gain appeared on Farm B, where the silty clay loam drained fastest
between irrigation events.

## Study Overview

Project Meridian investigated whether continuous soil moisture sensing could
reduce water use without lowering crop yield on medium-sized farms. The study
ran for 13 weeks, from June 2 to August 29, 2025, across three farms in the
central valley region.

## Statistical Analysis

Data were analysed with a mixed-effects model treating farm as a random
effect and irrigation strategy as a fixed effect. The yield difference was
significant at p < 0.01. A sensitivity analysis excluding the heatwave week
reduced the yield improvement estimate to 8.2%, which remains significant at
p < 0.05.

## Equipment

Each managed plot was fitted with an SM-100 soil dielectric moisture sensor
buried 25 cm deep in the root zone. The sensor recorded volumetric water
content every 15 minutes and transmitted readings over LoRaWAN to a local
gateway. Control plots were irrigated on the farm's traditional schedule with
no sensing equipment.

## 4. Connectivity

The Nebula Pro supports Wi-Fi 2.4 GHz (802.11 b/g/n), Bluetooth Low Energy 5.1
for proximity sensing, and Matter 1.2 for smart home integration. It works
with Google Home and Amazon Alexa ecosystems. Matter commissioning requires
the Nebula Home app version 4.0 or later. The device does not use the 5 GHz
Wi-Fi band; routers with band steering should create a separate 2.4 GHz SSID
during setup.

## 12. Factory Reset

To reset the Nebula Pro to factory settings, hold the rotary dial for 15
seconds until the LED flashes amber three times. Releasing the dial after
the amber pattern begins erases all schedules, Wi-Fi credentials, and the
calibration history. A factory reset does not deregister the device from the
Nebula Home app; use the "remove device" option for that.

## 6. Warranty

Every Nebula Pro carries a 3-year limited warranty from the date of purchase.
The warranty covers defects in materials and workmanship under normal
residential use. To activate the full coverage, register the device in the
Nebula Home app within 30 days of purchase. Damage caused by incorrect
wiring, water ingress, or third-party accessories is excluded.

## 14. Companion App

The Nebula Home app is required for Wi-Fi setup and remote control. It is
available for iOS 16 and later and Android 12 and later. The app stores
temperature history for 12 months and supports geofencing, so the heating
drops to the away temperature when the last household member leaves.

## 1. Product Overview

The Nebula Pro Smart Thermostat is a wall-mounted climate controller designed
for residential heating systems. It combines a rotary dial with a 4-inch
touchscreen and learns the household's routine over a two-week calibration
period. The unit is manufactured by Halcyon Home Systems and sold through
authorised retailers and the Halcyon online store.

## 11. Sensors and Accuracy

The built-in temperature sensor is accurate to plus or minus 0.3 degrees
Celsius, and the humidity sensor to plus or minus 2 percent. Two remote

detected.

Installation takes approximately 30 minutes. The mounting procedure is:
switch off the heating circuit, label the existing wires, attach the wall
plate, connect the wires to the labelled terminals, and clip the display unit
onto the plate. The thermostat automatically detects the connected system
type during first power-on.

## 3. Electrical Requirements

The Nebula Pro is designed for low-voltage HVAC systems only. It must be
connected to 24 VAC power and requires a C-wire (common wire). It is NOT
compatible with high-voltage systems running 110 V or 240 V mains directly.
Installing the unit on a high-voltage circuit will permanently damage the
device and voids the warranty. A licensed electrician should perform the
installation if a C-wire is not present at the thermostat location.

## 9. Scheduling

The Nebula Pro supports up to eight temperature schedules per day, each with
its own target temperature. Schedules can be copied between weekdays and
weekends in the app. A holiday mode holds a fixed temperature for a chosen
number of days.
